lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The prophet Nathan came to the king with a story about a poor man who had one little ewe lamb, and a rich man who took it from him and killed it for his guest.

lines.speaker: nathan
lines.text: The rich man had many flocks and many herds. Yet he took the poor man's only lamb and slew it. What shall be done to him?

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: As the LORD lives, the man who has done this deserves to die. He shall make restitution fourfold.

lines.speaker: nathan
lines.text: You are the man. You have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite and killed him with the sword of the Ammonites.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: David's mouth went dry. The prophet had not spoken against the king in public. He had spoken to the king in private, as a man to a man.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I have sinned against the LORD. Nathan, the LORD has put away my sin. I shall not die.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The child died, and the king fasted and wept. When the mourning was over, David went in to Bathsheba and comforted her, and she bore a son.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: The king could have silenced the prophet. Instead he listened, and the broken place became the place from which a new child — and a new song — would grow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The child was named Solomon, and the LORD loved him. Nathan spoke to the boy of wisdom and of a house that would be built without hands.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Teach him, Nathan. Let him hear the truth of what his father was and of what the LORD has made of him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: David's repentance did not erase the past. It changed what the past would become: a testimony that mercy follows the man who owns his failure.

choices.label: Let the story be told honestly
choices.note: A king who can name his sin is a king who can be trusted with the truth.

choices.label: Keep the failure buried with the dead
choices.note: Some silences protect a throne. They do not protect a soul.
